review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its uses with Grep. The file has two @[simp] lemmas, `weightedTranslationResidueQuotientMap_mk` and `weightedTranslationResiduePhaseQuotientMap_mk`. Each rewrites a map applied to `QuotientGroup.mk g` into `QuotientGroup.mk (bchRealTranslationHom ...)`. The right-hand side is smaller and cannot be rewritten by either lemma again, so there is no cycle. The two lemmas have different head symbols, so they do not compete. The phase map is a plain `def` alias, so simp does not unfold it, and that is why it needs its own `_mk` lemma. The only external use I found is in `WeightedTranslationTwistedNiltest.lean`. There, `weightedTranslationTwistedObservable_mk` is proved by `rfl` and is itself a simp lemma, so the phase-map `_mk` lemma is already part of a consistent simp interface. The theorems `bchRealTranslationHom_rational_residue` and `realResidueLattice_translation_residue_map` are membership facts, and I do not think they should be simp lemmas. I found no missing canonical simp rule, wrong orientation or unwanted expansion. The `simp` calls inside the proofs are ordinary local uses, and I had no evidence of a problem with them. I could not run Lean, so the absence of problems is judged from the source text alone.
